research_question: Which new expressions and shifted senses occur in a specified English community corpus during the declared collection period?
inclusion_criteria: Include lexical, morphological and semantic neologism candidates, including a familiar spelling used with a community-specific sense.
Retain singleton discoveries and contradictory proposed senses with their exact evidence; investigate historical novelty separately.
exclusion_criteria: Exclude proper names used only as names, ordinary unchanged senses, and incidental typos without contextual use.
Do not infer coinage dates, widespread adoption or historical novelty from an extraction or retrieval date.

positive.text: Residents use ice for a petrol car occupying an electric-vehicle charging space.
positive.sense: a petrol car occupying an electric-vehicle charging space
positive.reason: SYNTHETIC GUIDE EXAMPLE. Synthetic illustration of a shifted sense discussed in NEO-BENCH; actual research needs its own observed context.

negative.text: Ice melted in the kitchen sink.
negative.reason: SYNTHETIC GUIDE EXAMPLE. An unchanged everyday sense is outside this proposed neologism policy.

boundary.text: The writer calls doomscrolling a habit of repeatedly reading upsetting news.
boundary.reason: SYNTHETIC GUIDE EXAMPLE. A plausible term candidate is not evidence of recent coinage; independently research chronology.

innovation_type.description: Suggested lexical, morphological or semantic innovation; a human must confirm novelty.

novelty_evidence_note.description: Suggested evidence needed to investigate historical novelty; never fabricate external evidence.

specialist_lenses.lens: Attend to new forms, compounds and morphological innovations in the declared community.
Attend to familiar forms with new senses; compare the expression with its exact local context.
